examples.en: I subscribe to a newspaper every morning.
I subscribed to my favorite channel.
Many people subscribe to this magazine.

examples.ko: 구독하면 새 영상이 올라올 때 알림이 와요.
examples.en: If you subscribe, you get a notification when a new video is posted.
I will subscribe for just one month.
If you do not use a service you subscribed to, cancel it.

explain: 구독하다는 신문·잡지처럼 정기적으로 받아 보려고 신청할 때 쓰고, 요즘은 유튜브 채널이나 음악·영상 서비스에도 써요. '구독하다'의 목적어는 '채널을', '신문을'처럼 '을/를'이에요. 그만둘 때는 '구독을 취소하다', '구독을 해지하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 구독하다 means signing up to receive something regularly, like a newspaper or magazine, and today also YouTube channels and music or video services. The object takes 을/를, as in '채널을 구독하다'. To stop, say '구독을 취소하다' or '구독을 해지하다'.

examples.en: The government decided to raise interest rates.

examples.ko: 이 약은 체온을 상승시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine can raise body temperature.
A good ad pushed sales up.
Exercise lifts your mood.
If you raise the price, customers decrease.

examples.ko: 회사의 가치를 상승시킨 사람은 새 대표예요.
examples.en: The person who raised the company's value is the new CEO.

explain: '올리다'와 가깝지만 더 딱딱해서 뉴스, 경제, 보고서에 어울려요. 저절로 오르는 것은 '상승하다', 올리는 사람이 있으면 '상승시키다'예요. 반대말은 '하락시키다'예요.
explain_en: It is close to '올리다' but stiffer, so it suits news, economics, and reports. Something that rises by itself is '상승하다'; when someone causes the rise, use '상승시키다'. The opposite is '하락시키다'.

examples.en: The company became a sponsor of the competition.
We could not find a sponsor, so the event was scaled down.

examples.ko: 스폰서 덕분에 무료로 열 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the sponsor, we could hold it for free.

examples.ko: 이 팀의 스폰서는 유명한 음료 회사예요.
examples.en: This team's sponsor is a famous beverage company.
We passed on our thanks to the sponsor.
We signed a contract with a new sponsor.

explain: '후원자', '후원하다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 방송이나 행사에서는 '협찬'이라는 말도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 'Huwonja' and 'huwonhada' are used too. In broadcasts and events you also see the word 'hyeopchan'.

examples.ko: 공사 현장 일꾼은 숙식을 제공받아서 월급을 거의 모았다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the construction workers got room and board, so they saved almost all their pay.
I get lunch provided by my company.
I was provided with a laptop by my school.

examples.ko: 이 앱으로 실시간 교통 정보를 제공받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this app you can receive real-time traffic information.

examples.ko: 무료로 제공받은 쿠폰은 이번 달까지 써야 해요.
examples.en: The coupon I got for free has to be used by the end of this month.

examples.ko: 서비스를 제공받으려면 먼저 회원 가입을 하세요.
examples.en: To receive the service, please sign up as a member first.

explain: 주는 쪽은 '제공하다', 받는 쪽은 '제공받다'예요. '회사에서 숙소를 제공받다'처럼 '-에서/-에게 ~을 제공받다'로 써요. 말할 때는 '(무료로) 받다'로 바꿔도 되지만 '제공받다'가 공식적인 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '제공하다' is for the giver and '제공받다' is for the receiver. Use it like '회사에서 숙소를 제공받다', with -에서/-에게 marking the source. In casual speech you can say '(무료로) 받다' instead, but '제공받다' sounds more formal.

examples.en: Exercise increases strength.
The company increased production this year.

examples.ko: 홍보를 늘리면 손님을 증가시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you do more promotion, you can bring in more customers.
They say vitamins boost immunity.
I oppose policies that raise taxes.
I increased practice time, and my skills improved.

explain: 사람이나 원인이 직접 양을 늘리는 쪽이에요. 스스로 늘어난 것은 '증가하다', 누가 늘린 것은 '증가시키다'라고 해서 짝이 돼요. 일상에서는 '늘리다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Here a person or cause directly makes an amount grow. It pairs with '증가하다' for things that grow on their own. In everyday speech, '늘리다' sounds more natural.
